description: Every claim matches the fact sheet.
narrative: Sessions rose 16.2% week over week while signups declined 10.1%. Revenue climbed 7.9% and cost increased 7.5%. Cost per signup rose 19.6%, and the conversion rate softened.

description: Signups are DOWN; narrative says they grew.
narrative: Sessions rose 16.2% week over week and signups grew as well. Revenue climbed and cost increased.

description: Cost per signup went UP (worse). 'Improved' on a lower-is-better metric means DOWN, so this is wrong.
narrative: Cost per signup improved this period, landing at $43.88.
Cost per signup worsened, rising 19.6% to $43.88.
Sessions were up 26% compared with the prior week.

description: Rounded percent within 1.5 points is accepted.
narrative: Sessions were up 16% compared with the prior week.

description: Each direction word attaches to the nearest preceding metric.
narrative: Revenue climbed while cost per signup rose, a mixed result.
Revenue climbed while cost per signup fell, a strong result.

description: 'conversion rate of 3.2%' is a level, not a change; must not be flagged.
narrative: The conversion rate came in at 3.2%, down from the prior period.

description: 'to 3.2% from 4.1%' are both levels of a percent-unit metric; only '22.6%' is a change claim.
Signups are DOWN. 'did not grow' is a correct (negated) claim and must not be flagged.
narrative: Signups did not grow this week.

description: Sessions are UP. 'didn't increase' is a negated up-claim, i.e. down, which is wrong.
narrative: Sessions didn't increase compared with last week.

description: 'not flat' says it moved but not which way; the validator makes no claim rather than guessing.
narrative: Revenue was not flat this period.

description: Percent precedes its metric ('a 16.2% rise in sessions') after a different metric; must attach forward, not to revenue.
narrative: Revenue climbed 7.9%, and a 16.2% rise in sessions followed.

description: Same structure, hallucinated number — must still be caught against the forward metric.
narrative: Revenue climbed 7.9%, and a 30% rise in sessions followed.

description: KNOWN LIMITATION: spelled-out numbers ('sixteen percent') are not parsed, so a wrong value passes. Documented, not yet handled.
KNOWN LIMITATION: a direction word with no metric in the sentence ('It fell sharply.') cannot be attributed and is skipped.
narrative: Sessions set a new high. It fell sharply.
A busier period overall. The team should review next week.
